summary: A Binary Search Tree (BST) is a binary tree where left subtree keys are smaller and right subtree keys are larger than the node's key. Search, insertion, and deletion operations take O(h) time, depending on tree height h. In a balanced BST, operations take O(log n) time, while a skewed tree resulting from sorted insertions takes O(n) time. Inorder traversal visits keys in ascending order. Deletion handles leaf nodes, nodes with one child, and nodes with two children using their inorder successor. Self-balancing trees like AVL trees use rotations to maintain a height close to log2(n).
